plan.topic: Is there an approved GLP-1 patch? Real semaglutide and tirzepatide microneedle patches are still in development as of Oct 2026
plan.angle: Title: 'Is There an Approved GLP-1 Patch Yet? (As of Oct 2026) #shorts'. Opening line by 10 s: 'Is there an approved GLP-1 patch? Not yet, as of Oct 2026.' Explain that semaglutide is a big peptide that the skin barrier mostly keeps out, so researchers are testing microneedle patches. Example: Daewoong's semaglutide patch is in early (phase 1) testing in Korea, and the company is aiming for manufacturing-site (GMP) approval in H1 2027, which is not drug approval. Patches sold online as 'GLP-1 patches' aren't the approved medicines. FDA warns about unapproved GLP-1 products. Better route: ask your prescriber about approved pill or injection options. No tirzepatide patch claim, no seller, no product shots. Close with the prescriber line.

plan.why: Myth-busts about unapproved online products work for us (online-retatrutide Short 56, 'cures online' Short 82). Competition is low and search pages are just appearing. | fact-check: Verified: Daewoong is targeting H1 2027 GMP approval of a microneedle facility (Hwaseong) to make DWRX5003, a once-weekly semaglutide patch (Korea Biomedical Review idxno=33474; Korea Herald). Korea's MFDS cleared a phase 1 trial in Oct 2025. The GMP target is for manufacturing clinical-trial supply and, later, commercial supply. It is NOT a product approval, so say so. The company-reported '>80% bioavailability vs injection' is a company claim. Use it only if credited and labelled early-stage, or leave it out. A separate semaglutide microarray patch study (VX-201 vs subcutaneous injection, NCT07673900) is listed on ClinicalTrials.gov. I could not verify any tirzepatide patch developer. Search results were dominated by gray-market seller pages, so drop the tirzepatide developer line entirely. Myth-bust format fits the playbook (online 'retatrutide' 56). Never show, name or describe sellers, and don't show realistic product imagery. Cite FDA's 'FDA's concerns with unapproved GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss' page directly (verify the canonical URL at script stage).

package.title: Is There an Approved GLP-1 Patch Yet? (Oct 2026) #shorts
package.description:
Quick answer: No GLP-1 patch is approved as of Oct 2026. Semaglutide is a large peptide skin doesn't easily absorb, so microneedle patches are still being tested. A Korean semaglutide patch was cleared to start a phase 1 safety trial in Oct 2025.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
- FDA, "FDA's Concerns with Unapproved GLP-1 Drugs Used for Weight Loss" (2026)
- Korea Biomedical Review, "Daewoong targets H1 2027 GMP approval for semaglutide microneedle patch production" (2026)
- Prausnitz MR, "Microneedles for transdermal drug delivery," Advanced Drug Delivery Reviews (2004)
- Bos JD, Meinardi MM, "The 500 Dalton rule for the skin penetration of chemical compounds and drugs," Experimental Dermatology (2000)

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe to publish. I found five minor problems, mostly source tags and one title, and none of them changes a claim.

Checked against the sources:
- **Daewoong's semaglutide patch (Korea Biomedical Review, published Oct 14, 2026):** the article backs every claim in s4 and s5. DWRX5003 is a once-weekly semaglutide patch for obesity. Korea's drug regulator (MFDS) cleared a phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetics trial in healthy adults in October 2025. The company is aiming for factory (GMP) approval in the first half of 2027. It plans a repeat-dose phase 1 trial in 2027 and gave no date for drug approval or launch.
- **FDA page (now at /drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/, "content current as of 10/01/2026"):** it says unapproved versions "do not undergo FDA's review for safety, effectiveness and quality before they are marketed", which matches s6. The page never mentions patches.
- **Size claim (s2):** semaglutide weighs about 4,114 Da. The 500 Dalton rule (Bos & Meinardi, Exp Dermatol 2000, PMID 10839713) gives about 8× the usual limit.
- **Microneedle review (s3):** Prausnitz, Adv Drug Deliv Rev 2004, PMID 15019749, is a real paper.

Safety and framing:
- No dosing, no buying routes and no advice to stop or switch.
- The prescriber line is present.
- The hook pays off in the first line.
- The GMP twist is described correctly.
- About 150 words, under the 170-word cap.

Minor fixes:
1. The src5 title is out of date.
2. The s6 card and the s7 line are tagged to an FDA page that doesn't say what's attached to them.
3. s3's "researchers are testing" is tagged only to a general review from 2004.
4. The phase 1 population is missing from s4.
5. The channel cross-promo in s7 must point to a video that actually exists.

I couldn't load the PubMed or PubChem pages directly (cookie and captcha walls), so I confirmed both papers through search results instead.

issues.claim: Title: 'Daewoong targets GMP approval for microneedle plant to produce semaglutide patch DWRX5003'
issues.problem: This isn't the published title. The article is titled 'Daewoong targets H1 2027 GMP approval for semaglutide microneedle patch production' and was published Oct 14, 2026.
issues.fix: Set the src5 title to: "Daewoong targets H1 2027 GMP approval for semaglutide microneedle patch production" (Korea Biomedical Review, 2026).

issues.claim: 'No GLP-1 patch is FDA-approved as of Oct 2026' and 'Approved options today are injections, and semaglutide also comes as a pill', both tagged src1
issues.problem: The FDA page on unapproved GLP-1 drugs never mentions patches or pills, so it doesn't support either line. src5 shows the leading patch is still in phase 1. That makes the patch line our own conclusion, which shouldn't carry this tag.
issues.fix: s6: set source_ids to ["src1","src5"] and use src1 only for the narration line about FDA review. s7: remove src1 from the injections/pill line (use source_ids: []), or add the Wegovy tablet approval page from FDA or Novo Nordisk as a new source if you want a tag there.

issues.claim: 'Researchers are testing microneedle patches', tagged src4 (Prausnitz 2004)
issues.problem: src4 is a general microneedle review from 2004. It supports how microneedles work but not current GLP-1 patch testing.

issues.claim: 'cleared for an early phase 1 trial in October 2025'
issues.problem: The source says this was a safety and pharmacokinetics study in healthy adults. Naming that population makes it clearer how early-stage the patch is.
issues.fix: Narration: "In Korea, Daewoong's once-weekly semaglutide patch was cleared for a phase 1 safety trial in healthy adults in October 2025." Stat label: "safety trial in healthy adults, Korea, Oct 2025".

issues.claim: 'Our full tirzepatide versus semaglutide head-to-head breakdown is on our channel.'
issues.problem: I can't confirm this video exists. If it doesn't, the line promises something the channel doesn't deliver.
issues.fix: Keep the line only if the long-form is already published. Otherwise replace it with: "Our channel breaks down how the approved options work."

notes: Caption card 1 reads 'IS THERE AN APPROVED' — cuts off the noun phrase 'approved GLP-1 patch' on the adjective 'APPROVED', an orphaned fragment.
Caption splits into '~8X' then 'TIMES BIGGER THAN WHAT', ending on the question word WHAT with no question mark — reads as a dangling fragment and duplicates the stat pill awkwardly.
Caption 'OUTER LAYER MOSTLY' is a fragment with no verb, unclear what it's describing without the following card.
Caption 'POINTS THAT GET' ends on the verb GET with nothing completed — a classic mid-clause cut.
Caption card ends 'IN KOREA,' — trailing comma is an explicitly banned last token.
The clause is also presented out of order (location before the verb 'was cleared'), confusing on first read.
Caption 'FOR A PHASE' is a meaningless fragment on its own.
Caption spells out 'OCTOBER 2025' while the stat card above shows the abbreviation 'Oct 2025' — inconsistent date formatting.
Two consecutive caption cards both end on bare verbs/adjectives with no object: 'THE COMPANY IS AIMING' and 'IN THE FIRST' — neither is a readable clause on its own.
Caption card ends on the explicitly banned last word 'THE' ('THAT'S APPROVAL FOR THE'), leaving an unreadable fragment.

Caption 'THEY HAVEN'T PASSED' is cut before its object; the three-item list (Safety/Effectiveness/Quality) shown in the chips is then split awkwardly, with 'Safety' dropped from the caption text entirely.
Caption 'THE APPROVED OPTIONS' is a bare noun phrase with no completing verb visible in this card.
Caption 'DOWN HOW THE APPROVED' is garbled word-salad (missing lead word, likely 'BREAKING DOWN HOW THE APPROVED...'), unreadable as a standalone card.
An empty white speech bubble floats above the two characters with no text inside it — reads as a rendering mistake / placeholder.
Caption cards 'DOCTOR OR PRESCRIBER' and 'FOR YOU.' are each readable, no issue there.

audio.soundNotes: Trimmed clustered cues (opening second, ~14.3s, ~17.5s, ~37s, ~62s and ~72.2s each had 5–7 overlapping stock hits) down to 3–4 per second by dropping redundant duplicate layers (extra ticks/whips/blips/swooshes). Rescued three badly ducked-out swell/tick cues (32.5s, 53.5s, 57.5s) by pushing them to the 1.5x cap — still soft but audible — and pulled down three transients that read louder than the voice (33.4s, 54.2–54.6s, 58.4s). Music nudged down slightly (0.85x) since pause-level music was a bit hot (-10.2 dB) versus the under-voice level (-13.5 dB, already in range); this should land pauses nearer -14 dB without losing the under-voice feel. Added 5 bespoke accents for the patch concept, the Phase 1 reveal, the 'not yet / factory ≠ approval' caution beats, and a warm resolve on the final prescriber line, all kept subtle per the serious/cautionary tone of this script.
